title: Basic Web Recon: your first Docker lab
description: Spin up your first vulnerable lab with Docker and do real web reconnaissance with curl: robots.txt, hidden paths and talkative headers.

1.title: robots.txt and hidden paths
1.body:
## Spin up the lab

Use the command in the **Laboratory** panel on this page (above). When the container
is ready, check it:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:18080/
```

You should see the welcome page. Nothing sensitive… at first glance.

## robots.txt: the map that websites give away

`robots.txt` is a public file that tells search engines what NOT to index. The irony
is obvious: **you've just been handed the list of interesting places**.

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:18080/robots.txt
```

The `Disallow:` line contains a path. Visit it:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:18080/secreto/
```

Your first real lab flag is waiting there. Keep it for the final question of
this task.

> In a real pentest, robots.txt, sitemap.xml and backup files (`.old`, `.bak`,
> `.git/`) are the first stops of passive reconnaissance.

recon-web-basico-t01-q01.prompt: According to the lab's robots.txt, which path (starting with /) does it ask not to be indexed?

recon-web-basico-t01-q02.prompt: Visit that path with curl (or your browser) and submit the flag it contains.

2.title: Headers that say too much
2.body:
## The response says more than the body

HTTP response headers reveal information about the server (Server, X-Powered-By) and
sometimes contain **forgotten secrets**. Ask the server for just the headers:

```bash
curl -I http://127.0.0.1:18080/
```

Among the usual ones there's a custom `X-…` header that shouldn't be there.
The flag it contains is the final answer of this room.

## When you're done

ALWAYS destroy the lab when you finish:

```bash
docker compose -f labs/web-recon-1/compose.yaml --env-file labs/web-recon-1/flags.env down -v
```

Labs are ephemeral: spin up → practice → destroy. In your next session it will be
clean again.

recon-web-basico-t02-q01.prompt: Submit the flag hidden in the server's response headers.
recon-web-basico-t02-q01.hint: curl -I http://127.0.0.1:18080/ and look at the X-… headers
